designLab.title: Design lab
designLab.devOnly: Development only. Nothing here reaches the production build, and nothing you do here is saved. All data is sample data.
designLab.gone: There is no such variant. It may have been removed after a choice.

review.how: Click a picture to view it full screen. Use the left and right arrow keys to switch between the options, and Escape to close. Then answer in the chat with the letter.

projectPage.title: Project page
projectPage.question: Which layout should the page of one project use? All three use only data the server already has.
projectPage.outcome: Chosen: C, the guided next step (first picture).

options.name: Guided next step
options.summary: A three-step line and only the current step as one card. A new project sees 'Bring in your mod'.

options.name: Overview cards
options.summary: Three small cards side by side: the mod source, the Setup status and a button to the tasks.

options.name: Tabs
options.summary: Overview, Mod source, Setup and Tasks tabs. Only one area shows at a time.

projectList.title: Project list
projectList.outcome: Chosen: A, the minimal table, with a one-field empty state and no mascot.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.outcome: Chosen: C, revised to the cinematic blue panel with the mascot leaning in from the edge (first picture).

mascot.title: Mascot
mascot.outcome: Chosen: the original brick factory (first picture), with real eyes. It appears only for tips, tutorials and when called up.

assets.title: Icons and logo
assets.outcome: The icon set is used. The logo is the factory roof in an outline that follows the theme's text color.

targets.title: Target look for every page
targets.outcome: Approved as the target look. Each page round starts from these.

review.keys: Left and right arrows switch options. Escape closes.

provisional.kicker: Picked overnight, waiting for your OK
provisional.title: Choices made while you were away
provisional.body: You asked that work go on without waiting. For each page below I picked the option I recommend, built it and marked it provisional. Look through the options and tell me any page and letter you want instead, and I will switch it.

setup.title: Setup wizard
setup.question: How should the Setup wizard show its six steps?
setup.why: The maintainer chose vertical steps over the overnight horizontal pick.
setup.outcome: Chosen by the maintainer: vertical steps.

options.name: Vertical steps
options.summary: A narrow list of the six steps on the left and the current step on the right.

options.name: Horizontal stepper
options.summary: Numbered circles across the top of the Setup card, the current step below, earlier steps folded away.

options.name: One question at a time
options.summary: A narrow centered card with a progress bar and "step 4 of 6", nothing else.

tasks.title: Task list
tasks.question: How should a project's task list look?
tasks.why: The maintainer chose the table over the overnight grouped pick.
tasks.outcome: Chosen by the maintainer: the table with a side panel.

options.name: Table and side panel
options.summary: A full table with mode, state, spend and model, and the new task form in a panel on the right.

options.name: Grouped by state
options.summary: "Needs you" first, then "Working", with finished tasks folded away. New task opens a form under the title.

options.name: Ask first
options.summary: A large composer box at the top, like a chat, and a one-line list of tasks below it.

taskPage.title: Task page
taskPage.question: How should one task's page look while the agent works and after it finishes?
taskPage.why: The maintainer chose tabs over the overnight single-column pick.

options.name: Tabs
options.summary: Activity, Attempts, Permission and Settings tabs under the title.

options.name: Single-column story
options.summary: A status card with the state, a spend meter and the controls, then the live activity. Attempts and settings fold away.

options.name: Two columns
options.summary: The live activity timeline on the left, permission and settings cards on the right.

account.title: Account
account.question: How should the account page look?
account.why: The maintainer kept the overnight pick.
account.outcome: Chosen by the maintainer: stacked cards.

options.name: Stacked cards
options.summary: Your details, usage with a meter, model keys as quiet rows, and sessions, one card each in one column.

options.name: Settings list
options.summary: A small section menu on the left and plain settings rows on the right, no cards.

options.name: Usage first
options.summary: A large allowance panel on top, then model keys and account side by side.

focusEditor.title: Focus editor
focusEditor.question: Which minimal focus editor should be built? In all three the game render fills the page, you ask the agent in plain words and approve or reject what it did. You move a focus by dragging it. There are no number fields and no lists.

options.name: Just ask
options.summary: Only the tree and one bar: what the agent did, Approve or Reject, and the request box. No fields at all. Every change goes through the agent.

options.name: Ask, with a focus card
options.summary: The same bar. Clicking a focus also opens a small card where you can type its title, description and cost yourself.

options.name: Change list
options.summary: A narrow column beside the tree lists each thing the agent changed. Click a line to see it on the tree. The request box sits under the list.

changeCard.title: Change card
changeCard.question: How should the review of one proposal show the game render before it is approved? All four show the same few lines and the same two buttons.

options.name: Before and after side by side
options.summary: Both renders at the top, what changed under them, Approve and Discard in a bar at the bottom.

options.name: Two columns with a toggle
options.summary: What changed and the buttons on the left. On the right one render with an After and Before toggle.

options.name: Decision first with a slider
options.summary: What changed and the buttons first. Under them one render with a divider you drag to compare.

options.name: Render on top with tabs
options.summary: The render with an After and Before toggle on top. What changed and Details are tabs, the buttons beside them.

focusEditorDetailed.title: Focus editor, first round
focusEditorDetailed.outcome: None chosen. All four showed too much. The editor has to be far more minimal, with the agent doing most of the work.

components.title: Design system
components.subtitle: Workbench, the chosen direction: the real tokens, styles and shared components from ui.tsx, in every variant and state. Switch the theme in the bar above.
components.typeBody: Body text is 15 pixels on a desktop and 16 pixels in form fields on phones, so phones never zoom in on focus.
components.typeSmall: Small text, 13 pixels, for dates, hints and secondary details.
components.modelHint: The free monthly allowance pays for this model.
components.modeRead: Read only: the agent looks at the mod and reports back
components.modeEdit: Edit: the agent may change files
components.consent: Start a Git history for this mod if it has none
components.dialogBody: A modal confirmation on the native dialog element: focus stays inside, Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button that opened it.
components.shellBody: The sidebar holds the navigation, the game reference, the theme and the account. On phones it becomes a top bar with a Menu button. Every real page already uses it.
components.shellLink: Open the project list in the new shell (sample data)
components.tl2: Inspected the focus tree danube_focus: 38 focuses, no layout problems
components.mascotSays: Hi, I am your factory guide. In the tutorial I hop over to each feature and point at it.

screens.title: Screens on sample data
screens.body: The real pages, served sample API answers instead of the server, so every state can be seen and captured. Each link opens in this tab and stays on sample data until you choose "Leave sample data" in the corner.
screens.link: Open the real screens on sample data
